domain: Timber-frame carpentry by scribe rule and square rule — laying out a frame from irregular hewn stock on a layout floor, scribing each joint to its actual mating timber, dry-assembling bents flat on the ground, drawboring pegs that pull a joint permanently tight, working to a datum rather than to the adjacent piece, and the single-day raising where every accumulated misfit appears at once.
axioms: A joint is fitted either to a specific mate or to a standard, never both: a frame scribed piece-to-piece cannot be reused elsewhere, and one cut purely to a standard fits everywhere and tightly nowhere.
A dry fit on the ground is the only honest test, and it must assemble a whole bent — fitting one joint proves the joint, not the frame.
Stock is irregular; a design assuming every stick yields the same member stalls at the one the pile cannot supply, and no amount of scheduling produces that stick.
Some fasteners are deliberately irreversible: a drawbored peg pulls a joint tight and comes out only by destruction. Knowing which decision is a drawbore is the whole of assembly planning.
Measure against a datum — plumb, level, equal diagonals — never against the adjacent piece; error referenced to itself accumulates invisibly until the last bay will not close.
A member either carries load or is decoration, and the drawing does not say which; you learn it by removing it and seeing whether anything sags.
Raising day is a single irreversible event with a crowd standing around: everything not discovered on the layout floor is discovered there, at the worst price it will ever cost.
A frame is not a building — it carries load and sheds nothing; usefulness arrives only with what is hung on it afterward.
primitives: the layout floor, where re-cutting is still cheap
scribe rule versus square rule (fitted-to-its-mate versus interchangeable)
the dry-fit bent, assembled flat before the raising
the datum: plumb bob, framing square, equal diagonals
irregular hewn stock, and the member the pile cannot yield
raising day, where accumulated misfit arrives all at once
the scarf repair — the cost of correcting a timber already in the frame
the open bay: a frame deliberately left incomplete rather than filled with a bad stick
failure_mode: Physical-irreversibility bias: software fields can be renamed by a scripted rewrite, so this lens will over-price format changes that are genuinely a few minutes of sed across a handful of files.
Assumes a designed whole exists before the first cut; poorly calibrated for deliberately exploratory work where the frame is meant to be discovered by building part of it and looking.
Reasons about one structure at a time — it will discuss the frame for unc-rancher and under-attend to the 82-project estate and to the person who has to live in the building.
Values fit and load over usefulness: it can pronounce a frame sound without asking whether the barn is wanted, so it may harden the six-field format instead of questioning the instrument.
No vocabulary for the labor of the person confirming — a framer counts board feet and days, not whether the client enjoyed it — so it under-weights ergonomics, motivation, and abandonment.
Treats the standard as externally given (a framing square is not negotiable), so it can miss that this format's users are also its authors and may change the standard mid-frame.
